history.summary: 2016 Punggol condo a genuine 4-min/300m from Punggol MRT/LRT interchange, riding the Punggol Digital District tailwind with 6.7%/yr resale CAGR on a deep 131-txn base. But the 990 sqft footprint is a compact 3BR, PSF 1768 is at the project median (no discount), the $1.75M quantum is high for the small size, and reviews flag a busy/noisy junction — a Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: The location is good — 300m to Punggol MRT/LRT interchange and direct exposure to PDD growth — and the 6.7%/yr resale CAGR on 131 txns is solid. But the value case is weak for this specific unit: 990 sqft for a 3BR is compact (you are paying $1.75M for a small layout), PSF 1768 is essentially at the URA median (1756) so no entry discount, and the implied PSF is high relative to the unit's size. Reviews note the development sits on a busy, noisy junction with low-floor traffic noise, so stack/floor selection matters. Net: a fine Punggol connectivity play but priced full for a compact unit — balanced, not compelling.

history.summary: Honest, well-supported pricing (131 appreciation txns; age_adj +1.3%, cohort +2.2%) but the S$1,765 psf ask sits at the very top of the verified S$1,405-1,772 range — you're paying peak, not a discount. Good OCR location, but ~2.8% yield and full pricing make it a hold-and-watch, not a buy.
history.rating_rationale: Web-verified Parc Centros sold S$1,405-1,772 psf over 12 months (avg ~S$1,671), with the high S$1,772 set in Jan 2026 for a 463 sqft unit — the same small-1BR cohort as this 473 sqft listing. At S$1,765 psf the ask is effectively at the ceiling, consistent with the dossier's near-zero discount (age_adj +1.3%, psf_premium_vs_cohort +2.2%). Per v3.4 priors VALUE leads and there is no value edge here; D19/OCR is a favourable forward region (~+4%), but you're buying at peak PSF with a thin ~2.82% yield. Data is genuine (no quirk), which is why this is a confident Neutral rather than a quirk-driven discount.

history.summary: A ground-floor 1,324 sqft 3BR/2-bath at Parc Centros (Wee Hur, 2016 TOP, 618 units, 272m to Punggol NE17) asking $1.88M / $1,420psf. The -15% 'discount' to the project median is the ground-floor PES format, not value: the 2-bath count marks the liveable core as the project's compact ~990 sqft 3BR plus a ~330 sqft patio, and the only URA print of this exact 1,323.97 sqft format ever (Jun-26, floor 01-05) cleared at $1.92M / $1,450psf. The ask is ~2% below that one print. Fair price, sound project, weak carry, thin exit for the format.
history.rating_rationale: There is no real discount. Against its own format this ask is fair: the only exact-size print is Jun-26 $1.92M (fl 01-05, $1,450psf), and the listing is 2% below it. Against the liveable core it is a premium: compact 990 sqft 3BR/2-bath tower units cleared $1,738-1,787k in Mar-May 2026 ($1,756-1,787psf), and four are live now at $1.65-1.78M. So $1.88M pays ~$100-230k for a ground-floor patio that earns no extra rent and has one resale on record. The project itself is sound: 99.7% profitable on 294 resale pairs, a real MRT at 272m, OCR, a 10yr age that sits on the returns plateau and 86yr of lease. That is why this is not an Avoid. But the 822 score rests on psf_value +7.29 and age_value +6.67, which both come from the PES artifact, and the low-floor damper read 0 because there is no floor-level stack profile. Carry is ~1.6% net. At $1.88M it is also just over the 'his' $1.8M ceiling.
red_flags: The discount is the format. The -15.3% vs URA median and -8.5% vs the age-adjusted D19 median come from the ground-floor PES area. Tower 1,313 sqft units cleared $1,770-1,789psf (Dec-25, Aug-26). The only 1,323.97 sqft print ever is Jun-26 $1.92M / $1,450psf on floor 01-05, and the ask is just 2% under it.

3BR with only 2 baths at 1,324 sqft (662 sqft/bath). The mainstream 1,141-1,163 sqft 3BRs have 3 baths. This is the compact 990 sqft 3BR/2-bath core plus a ~330 sqft patio, so the liveable space is ~990 sqft.

Paying up for the patio. Four comparable 990 sqft 3BR/2-bath tower units are live at $1.65-1.78M, and recent prints are $1.74-1.77M (Mar-May 2026). The $100-230k premium buys outdoor space that adds nothing to rent and limits the exit buyer pool.
Thin exit for this format: 1 print out of 128 in the URA set. The project's 'very deep' buyer pool belongs to the 464-1,163 sqft tower stock.

Possible stale or already-sold listing. The id 500090317 is older than listings first seen in June 2026, yet the DB only picked it up on 2026-09-24. The one exact-size, low-floor print closed in Jun-26 at $1.92M. Confirm with the agent that the unit is still available and which unit it is before acting.
Weak carry. ura_project_bed rent is $4,200 (40 contracts), which gives 2.68% gross / ~1.58% net. realsmart's median rent is $3,490. Rent follows the 990 sqft core, not the patio.
Score artifact. psf_value +7.29 and age_value +6.67 drive the 822 and both come from the PES discount. low_floor = 0 because no stack profile exists, so the ground-floor defences could not fire.
The trailing 6.6% ura_5yr_cagr covers the 2021-22 post-COVID repricing (1,141 sqft went from $1,043-1,315 to $1,629-1,753psf). Momentum is -0.24. Do not read the CAGR as a forward rate.
Ground floor: less privacy, more noise from the common areas and pool, and a narrower buyer pool (mainly families with young kids or pets).
catalysts: A real MRT, not LRT: Punggol NE17 interchange at ~272m, plus Waterway Point mall next door.
OCR, the strongest realized forward region in the backtest (+3.7%/yr).

Strong project downside record: REALSCORE 4.0, 99.7% profitable (292 profitable vs 2 unprofitable on 294 matched resale pairs, 898 total transactions), 6.9yr average hold, 5.7% average annualized return, last print 27-Aug-2026. This says owners rarely lose money here; it is not a forecast.
Age 10, inside the 7-30yr returns plateau, with 86 years of lease left, so no financing or decay pressure over a 5-7yr hold.
Punggol Digital District and the Punggol North employment node. This is narrative only; the backtest gives future infrastructure zero measured forward power.
The large PES has real own-stay appeal for families, and that buyer is the exit, at this format's own price rather than the tower's.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Rent tracks the ~990 sqft 3BR/2-bath core. URA project 3BR rent is ~$4,200/mo (40 contracts, 12mo) and realsmart's median is $3,490 (range $2,750-5,700). Expect $3,800-4,300, or 2.4-2.7% gross / ~1.5% net at $1.88M. Punggol tenant demand is solid but the patio earns no rent premium.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Same-size tower resales ran from ~$1,315psf (2022) to ~$1,750psf (2026) for 1,141 sqft, mostly a 2021-23 regime move. Recent 2025-26 prints are flat to slightly up (1,141 sqft: $1,629 in Apr-25, $1,753 in Aug-26), and momentum is negative. Forward, expect roughly the OCR baseline, ~2.5-3.5%/yr. The PES format adds exit friction, not upside. No override: the data rate stands and the forward view is carried in this assessment.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists and /research-development was not run in this unattended pass. Floor = 'Ground Floor' (listing feed). Format is inferred from URA: 1,323.97 sqft sits between the 1,313 and 1,346 sqft tower 4BR/3BR formats but has 2 baths, which matches the ~990 sqft compact 3BR plus a PES. The only print of this size is floor 01-05, Jun-26, $1,450psf, versus $1,770-1,789psf for tower 1,313 sqft units on floors 06-10. The best stock in the project is mid/high-floor tower units, and this is the ground-floor patio tier. Facing is unknown.
